item.title: Bad News For Dolphins, Colts Defense Help Snap Five-Game Skid
item.description: Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Indianapolis finally found a way to win, but it was a messy job that required every ounce of luck the team could find against Miami. The Colts beat the Miami Dolphins 24-22 on Sunday at Lucas Oil Stadium to end a five-game losing streak that had fans screaming for answers. The offense did just enough to keep Miami in the game, but the defense delivered the only play that mattered when it counted. The victory marked the team’s first win since Week 4, according to Colts.com. It came after a long stretch where the unit looked lost and unable to stop anyone. The win stops the bleeding, but the path to get there showed how fragile this squad still is. They need more than just luck to survive the rest of the season. A Rare Defensive Spark The defense had been a major problem all year, sitting with just six takeaways heading into Week 10. That number was the second-lowest in the entire NFL, per Colts.com. Fans had waited weeks to see a big play from the back end, and it finally arrived in the most dramatic fashion possible. Cornerback Justin Walley forced a strip sack that defensive tackle Adetomiwa Adebawore recovered right in the end zone. That play marked the defense’s seventh turnover of the game and their first touchdown of the season, according to Colts.com. It was the kind of play that changes the momentum of a tight game. Without that score, the Colts likely lose this one. The offense struggled to move the ball consistently, so the defense had to do the heavy lifting to keep the team alive. Clutch Moments in the Fourth Miami refused to back down and cut the lead to just two points in the fourth quarter. The Colts found themselves in a tight spot again, relying on a rookie to make a play. According to Colts.com , rookie linebacker CJ Allen sacked Kyle McCord and forced the Dolphins back so far that a field goal attempt became impossible. That pressure forced a turnover on downs that ended the game and sealed the 24-22 victory. Rookie running back Seth McGowan scored in the end zone for the second time over the last two weeks, offering some assistance to the offense. Veteran wide receiver Laquon Treadwell also scored his first touchdown of the season, his first since Week 18 of 2021. Although the third-quarter score handed the Colts their first double-digit lead since Week 6, the team needed to hold on for dear life to maintain it. The teams now look ahead to their next matchups. item.title: Duncan claims maiden LPGA win with Annika victory
item.description: Lindy Duncan of the United States poses with the trophy after winning the first LPGA Tour title of her career in her 222nd start (Julio Aguilar) Lindy Duncan proved that perseverance pays off after capturing the first LPGA Tour title of her career with a two-shot victory at The Annika in Florida on Sunday. Duncan, 35, snagged her maiden LPGA title in her 222nd start after shooting a closing three-under-par 67 at Pelican Golf Club in Belleair to finish on 16 under. That left the journeywoman professional from Fort Lauderdale two shots clear of South Korea's Choi Hye-jin, who finished on 14 under after a final-round 68. Another South Korean, Ryu Hae-ran, shared third place with Japan's Yuri Yoshida on 13 under with Spain's Julia Lopez Ramirez in fifth on 12 under. Duncan's rollercoaster final round saw her open with two birdies either side of a bogey on the second, before she added another birdie on the seventh. A bogey on 12 dropped her to 14 under but back-to-back birdies down the stretch on the 16th and 17th ultimately proved decisive. "I'm just still kind of speechless," Duncan said afterwards as she reflected on her long journey to a first title. "Don't really know what to say. 222 starts. That's a long time. That's kind of a cool number, so I kind of like that." Duncan later thanked friends and family for encouraging her to continue playing during the darkest moments of her career. "I think a lot of people were believing in me even when I was starting to lose the belief in myself," she said. "And they encouraged me to work on the right things and to open my mind and to be open to change because they could see the way that I was playing was not from a place of joy or freedom. "It was from a very tense place. I was very hard on myself and still have to work on that like every day." rcw/amz

item.title: Oklahoma State football had more issues than Drew Mestemaker's shoulder vs Texas Tech
item.description: STILLWATER — On Oklahoma State ’s first drive, a near worst-case scenario unfolded. On third-and-9, OSU coach Eric Morris called a screen play to receiver Miles Coleman. A wet football slipped through the fingers of Drew Mestemaker , who hunched to recover the snap. All 300 pounds of Texas Tech defensive lineman A.J. Holmes Jr. barged unblocked through OSU’s pulling offensive line and took a free run at Mestemaker, burying the quarterback’s right shoulder into the rain-soaked turf. On the sideline, Mestemaker rotated his shoulder, testing its range of motion. Postgame, he called the injury a stinger. It was a bad start to a subpar night for OSU’s offense. The unit that has carried OSU to victory this season five times by scoring more than 40 failed to move the ball consistently and score points in a 52-27 loss to Texas Tech . All 20 points OSU’s starting offense scored came in the second quarter. More: Oklahoma State football defense flunks test in ugly loss to Texas Tech | Report card The Cowboys scored 66 points last week against Kansas State, 49 against Iowa State the week before and 57 against Colorado. Saturday was the first time since the season-opener OSU’s offense was held below 30 points. Mestemaker’s streak of eight consecutive 300-yard passing games ended. He finished 27 of 42 for 277 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions and was pulled with 8:07 left after Texas Tech took a four-score lead. Mestemaker's injury impacted the game. The quarterback would brush it off in the postgame press conference, but his news conference was delayed because he had to first visit the training staff. “I don't think it compressed the playbook,” Mestemaker said. “I just landed on my shoulder weird and it was just a stinger. They were just trying to work me, keep the shoulder warm and just keep it feeling good out there.” OSU’s problems Saturday were bigger than one shoulder injury. Morris credited Texas Tech’s defense. He called the game “an old-fashioned butt whooping.” OSU’s offensive line got beat consistently throughout the night. Mestemaker was sacked three times and hit many more. One thing’s for sure, though: high-major and mid-major teams alike are not safe from this year’s Tigers. After taking down then-No. 18 Iowa State in Sioux Falls last week, Memphis routed No. 10 Louisville at home on Sunday, 98-78. Even more impressive than the 20-point victory over a top-10 ACC opponent was how it happened. Louisville looked early on like it might be off to a rout of its own, opening up a 20-4 lead within six minutes and leading by as much as 18. Louisville still held a 50-36 lead with under a minute to play in the first half. From there, it was all Memphis, which outscored the visitors 62-28 the rest of the way. Tylin Weeks and Jayden Reid led all scorers with 24 points apiece; each scored 18 points as part of the second-half blitz. “You can’t beat Louisville if you don’t have a good group. Especially by 20 when you were down 18,” Tigers’ head coach Penny Hardaway said after the game, per Memphis beat writer Jason Munz . “For me, we have something special.” The extended run was kick-started by a four-point play near the end of the first half by Brandon Cummings, who finished with eight points. The Tigers came out of the locker room on a 15-3 run, capped off by a Rihard Vavers triple, to secure their first lead since the early going at 56-55. item.title: World Series Champion Milwaukee Brewers Acquire Former Dominant Closer in Trade (Breaking News)
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers aren’t wasting any time trying to improve their roster following their historic 2026 World Series championship. On Sunday, Milwaukee acquired veteran right-handed relief pitcher Ryan Walker from the San Francisco Giants in exchange for minor league right-handers Blake Holub and Gavin Perry. The trade, initially reported by MLB insider Bob Nightengale, was subsequently confirmed by the Brewers . For a team coming off the ultimate achievement in baseball, the move represents an intriguing gamble on a pitcher who was among the National League’s most effective relievers just two seasons ago. Walker struggled mightily in 2026, but Milwaukee is betting there is still plenty left in the 30-year-old’s arm. And considering the Brewers ‘ track record of finding value in overlooked pitchers, it’s the type of move that could end up looking much better than it does on paper. Mandatory Credit: D. Ross Cameron-Imagn Images Milwaukee Brewers Acquire Ryan Walker From San Francisco Giants The Brewers announced the trade Sunday evening, confirming that Walker would be joining the organization in exchange for two minor league pitchers. Walker, who turns 31 on November 26, spent his first four major league seasons with San Francisco. Across 226 appearances, including 14 starts, he compiled a 20–15 record with a 3.56 ERA and 31 saves. Those career numbers are respectable, but they don’t fully illustrate how dominant Walker was at his best. In 2024, the right-hander emerged as one of the most effective relief pitchers in baseball. He finished that season with a 10–4 record, a 1.91 ERA and 10 saves across 76 appearances. Walker also struck out 97 batters in 79 innings, held opposing hitters to a .178 batting average and posted a remarkable 0.85 WHIP. That performance established him as a legitimate late-inning weapon. It’s also the version of Walker the Brewers will undoubtedly hope to rediscover. Those numbers represented a dramatic decline from his earlier success. His command became a particular concern, with walks and hard contact contributing to an increasingly difficult season. San Francisco optioned Walker to Triple-A multiple times as the organization searched for answers.

item.title: ‘We get this win’ – Watch Fernando Mendoza’s inspiring speech moments before Raiders debut
item.description: Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images Fernando Mendoza gave an inspiring pre-game speech before making his first NFL start for the Las Vegas Raiders. The rookie quarterback fired up his teammates ahead of a difficult matchup against the Seattle Seahawks. Mendoza shouted: “Here we f—— go. Everybody get together. Do your f—— job. And here we go. We get this win together because we love each other. We don’t care about them. We care about us. We care about together. Win on three. One, two, three, win.” “We get this win” was a bold prediction given the challenge awaiting Mendoza, but his confidence and enthusiasm were certainly encouraging. The 23-year-old’s speech also had shades of Kirk Cousins, who spent the opening nine weeks of the season mentoring him as the Raiders’ starting quarterback. Las Vegas selected Mendoza first overall in this year’s draft but initially opted to ease him into the NFL rather than throw him straight into the starting lineup. Cousins performed well during his spell as starter before the Raiders traded him back to his former team, the Minnesota Vikings. Mendoza therefore had a tough assignment for his first start, facing a Seattle defence capable of making life difficult for any quarterback. The former Indiana Hoosiers quarterback made a few mistakes and took some heavy hits, but showed plenty of promising moments. item.title: Stewart Cink makes it a back-to-back double-double at Charles Schwab Cup
item.description: PHOENIX ― History was made at Phoenix Country Club on Sunday as Stewart Cink went back-to-back winning not only the final event of the season, the Charles Schwab Cup Championship, but also claiming the season-long Charles Schwab Cup. Call it a back-to-back double double. Cink is the first golfer to pull off the twin wins in consecutive years. But this one didn't come without some tense moments on a day of sunny skies and warm temperatures. He started the final round with a three-shot lead over Scott Hend and good buddy Zach Johnson and quickly birdied the first hole. He also birdied the fourth but then posted bogeys on Nos. 6 and 9, which left him at even par on the day making the turn. Meanwhile, Johnson, who started Sunday tied for second while three shots back and playing in the twosome just ahead of Cink, strung together a bunch of pars before making birdies on Nos. 7 and 10, and suddenly it was a one-shot lead. Just two days prior, Cink led Johnson by seven but now things were getting interesting. Johnson had a shot at forging a tie for the lead but he just missed a birdie putt on 13. That kept him at 16 under, one shot back five holes to go. On the par-3 15th, Johnson stuffed his tee shot to about six feet but missed yet another birdie putt that would have tied things. Moments later, after hitting his approach on the 14th to about seven feet, Cink drained a birdie putt of his own to get to 18 under and open up a little breathing room with four to go. Cink dodged some trouble on 15 after missing the green. He had to chip over a bunker and his ball slid past the hole by about 4 feet but he then curled one in from the right side of the cup to save par. Cink's lead then went to three after he birdied the 16th while Johnson was making another par at the 17th. Johnson would finally make birdie at 18 to get to 17 under and sign for a final-round 68. As for Cink, he tapped in from a foot to seal the deal, shooting a final-round 2-under 69 to finish at 19 under and yet another Schwab title. A year ago, Cink became just the fourth golfer to claim the two Schwab titles in the same season – Tom Watson (2005), Tom Lehman (2012), Kevin Sutherland (2017) – and now he's the first to turn pull off that feat in consecutive years. He led in the points race for all of 2026 and only for about 24 hours after Friday's round in Phoenix was he even projected out of the top spot. Cink also won the 2026 money title, becoming the first to surpass $4 million in earnings in a single season on the PGA Tour Champions. item.title: Patrick Mahomes Ended a TD Drought as Chiefs Beat The Falcons
item.description: Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs had quite a day on Sunday. With Mahomes leading the attack, Kansas City took the Atlanta Falcons to the woodshed, showing the NFC South team what a real Super Bowl contender looks like. Mahomes had a game to remember against Atlanta, which struggled all game long to find a way to slow down the Chiefs at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta. The three-time Super Bowl champion quarterback threw not just one, not two, not three, not four but five touchdowns with zero interceptions on 22/35 pass completions. Mahomes was also well protected, as he was sacked just once for a loss of nine yards. Even without star running back Kenneth Walker III , who was ruled out before the game with an injury, Kansas City’s attack overpowered the host team. Emmett Johnson filled in nicely for Walker, with the rookie running back burning rubber for 101 rushing yards on 22 carries, while also adding 70 receiving yards and two scores on six receptions and seven targets. item.title: How Mizzou basketball woke up Jason Crowe Jr., pulled off comeback vs Marquette
item.description: CHICAGO — Jason Crowe Jr. was trying to pull a fast one on his head coach. With 13 minutes, 24 seconds left on the gameclock, after riding the bench for the previous four minutes while Missouri basketball tried to dig itself out of a double-digit hole, Crowe tried to slip past Dennis Gates while the coach was making substitutions. Gates, even with his team trailing by six points, was having nothing of the sort from his star freshman point guard. The head coach grabbed Crowe’s arm and sent him back to his seat. Crowe sat there for another two minutes. “He knew I called somebody else. His little behind wanted to get back in the game. He thought I was going to let him go, and I pulled him back. He wanted to get back in the game, but he needed to watch some things,” Gates said. … “He's just ready to play. He looks at me with little puppy dog eyes when I look down. … I pointed at one person, gave him the nod, and he just ran trying to get an opportunity to get back in the game.” Crowe’s time came, and he didn’t waste it. “That's his way of saying, ‘Coach, I'm ready to go,’” Gates said. Missouri basketball staged a remarkable comeback win over Marquette on Sunday at United Center, beating the Golden Eagles 69-64 after looking down and out for most of the neutral-site contest. More: Mizzou basketball erases big deficit, defeats Marquette as Crowe closes strong The Tigers trailed the Golden Eagles by 11 points in the second half. But they’ve got a five-star freshman to help with sticky situations like that. Crowe went from lethargic to lethal in the game’s closing stretch. One catch-and-shoot 3-point shot and, with 49 seconds remaining, a turn-and-shoot triple that gave the Tigers the lead for good. A contested mid-ranger. A backdoor cut into a layup, and-1. Nowhere was safe from the free-scoring freshman once he turned it on. He finished with 17 points. Of those, 13 came in the final six minutes and 30 seconds of the game. Quite the turnaround. item.description: In a showdown of two first-time boys soccer state finalists , central Ohio’s representative got its championship. Fairbanks thoroughly dominated the Division V final Nov. 15 at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field , getting goals from its top two offensive threats – sophomore forward Ty Schroeder and senior midfielder Kaden Procuniar – in a 4-0 win over Creston Norwayne that did not always feel that close. Schroeder scored his team-leading 34th goal in the bottom center of the net with 32:15 left on the Panthers’ 13th shot of the game. Three minutes later, Procuniar netted his 11th goal of the year. Norwayne (17-5-1) did not muster a shot until the 49th minute, when Lysander Bauman’s try was stopped by senior goalie Drew Sorg. That was Sorg’s only save of the game. item.title: Teenager Andreeva caps stunning week with WTA Finals title
item.description: Mirra Andreeva is the third teenager to win the WTA Finals singles trophy on debut at the tournament [Getty Images] For Mirra Andreeva, the thought of her first WTA Finals singles campaign was so stressful that it gave her "a little breakdown" in a practice session before the tournament. The 19-year-old may have been nervous on arrival at Indian Wells, but she leaves California as the champion, having been the standout player of the week. The French Open winner produced a hard-fought 7-5 6-3 victory over Elina Svitolina in Sunday's final to become the youngest champion of the event in 22 years. The Russian has now risen to second in the world rankings - and she will start the 2027 season just 293 points behind top-ranked Elena Rybakina. Andreeva did not drop a set on her way to the title and lost only 26 games across her five matches. She raised her arms in celebration after beating Svitolina before racing to celebrate with her team, which includes 1994 Wimbledon champion Conchita Martinez. "I am super thankful to my team for pushing me to my limits, for forcing me to do stuff when I don't want to do anything," Andreeva said. "Thanks for fighting with me, thanks for forcing me to do everything that I have to do and not asking any questions!" As well as £2.55m in prize money, Andreeva also won a custom purple Mercedes - and joked she was happy to remain a "passenger princess" until she passed her test. Andreeva thanks herself again after stellar season Mirra Andreeva is the youngest WTA Finals champion since a 17-year-old Maria Sharapova in 2004 [Getty Images] One of the most notable parts of Andreeva's performance has been her increased maturity. In March, she swore at the Indian Wells crowd after suffering an early defeat in the venue's WTA Tour tournament, and she has struggled to control her emotions on court in the past. However, she showed little sign of that during this tournament. Against Svitolina, one of the grittiest players on the women's tour, she lost a break lead three times across the two sets. Each time, she reset admirably, upping her aggression on her backhand in particular to put pressure back on her opponent. After losing serve in a mammoth nine-minute game in the second set, Andreeva marched back to her chair and then broke Svitolina from 40-0 down in the next game to stay in front. While her serve was not at its best, Andreeva still saved nine of the 12 break points she faced and hit 19 winners to Svitolina's 10. "This fighting mindset helped me to get more brave and aggressive in the important moments," Andreeva told Sky Sports. "This is just a dream. I had a little breakdown in my practice just before Indian Wells because I was so stressed. "I didn't want to lose a match in the group. It's amazing." Andreeva had only won one of her six matches against top-10 players in 2026 coming into the tournament.
